zh.title: 捷藍航空因人力短缺推出獎金 飛滿150小時給5000美元
zh.summary: 根據 Simple Flying 報導，捷藍航空因應人力短缺危機，本月將針對執飛150小時以上的空服員發放5000美元獎金。除了空服人力緊張之外，該航空公司近期也受到夏季嚴重雷雨氣候影響，面臨雙重營運挑戰。
body: 根據 Simple Flying 於2026年8月1日發布的報導，捷藍航空（JetBlue）針對本月執飛時數達150小時以上的空服員，提供5000美元的高額獎金。此舉旨在透過經濟獎勵激勵機組人員增加執飛時數，以緩減人力調度壓力。
捷藍航空近期持續面臨嚴重的人力短缺危機。在空服人力不足的情況下，航空公司試圖採取發放特別獎金的措施，鼓勵現有空服人員承擔更多航班任務。
除了內部人力吃緊之外，捷藍航空的航班營運同時面臨夏季嚴重雷雨氣候的干擾。惡劣天氣與人力不足互相加疊，對該公司的航班調度與營運穩定造成重大考驗。

en.title: JetBlue Offers $5,000 Bonus for Flight Attendants Flying 150-Plus Hours
en.summary: According to a report published by Simple Flying on August 1, 2026, JetBlue will pay its flight attendants a $5,000 bonus if they fly 150 or more hours within the month. The incentive policy is being implemented as JetBlue has been grappling with a severe staffing crisis. Additionally, the airline's flight operations have been impacted by severe summer thunderstorms, creating operational difficulties across its flight network during the summer season.
body: According to news published by Simple Flying on August 1, 2026, JetBlue has introduced a policy to pay flight attendants a bonus of $5,000 if they fly 150 or more hours during the current month. The incentive is aimed at maintaining flight schedules amid crew limitations.

JetBlue has been grappling with an ongoing staffing crisis that has impacted its flight operations. The carrier is seeking to encourage flight attendants to work additional flight hours in order to alleviate flight disruptions and crew scheduling bottlenecks.

In addition to staffing shortages, JetBlue's operations have been further strained by severe summer thunderstorms. Weather-related disruptions and manpower constraints have jointly presented major operational challenges for the airline.

zh.title: 波特航空升級Dash 8客艙使用全球最輕座椅
zh.summary: 波特航空正在其全數29架De Havilland Dash 8-400 turboprop客機上安裝Expliseat TiSeat 2V超輕量座椅，首批已投入服務，其餘預計於2026年秋季完成。座椅採碳纖維與鈦合金製造，聲稱重量比傳統經濟座減輕多達30%，同時提升燃油效益。機艙亦將加裝LED氛圍燈光、閱讀燈及新地毯，保持現有座距與2-2座佈局。
body: 波特航空宣布，將在全隊Dash 8-400客艙內更換為Expliseat TiSeat 2V超輕量座椅。這項改裝屬於機隊全面客艙現代化計畫，首批已升級的飛機已經投入服務，其餘飛機預計在2026年秋季前完成改裝。
Expliseat宣稱TiSeat 2V是其類別中的全球最輕飛機座椅，採用碳纖維與鈦合金結構，相較於傳統經濟座椅可減重多達30%。波特航空表示，減重將有助降低油耗與碳排放，特別適合Dash 8-400此類每日執行多個短航段的區域 turboprop。
除了座椅外，波特航空亦為Dash 8機隊加裝LED氛圍燈光、新式LED閱讀燈以及更換客艙地毯。機艙佈局保持不變，PorterReserve艙等級提供32吋座距，PorterClassic艙等級提供30吋座距，全機採用2-2座佈局，無中間座位。
波特航空執行副總裁暨營運長Kent Woodside指出，乘客反饋顯示座椅舒適度是旅行體驗的重要因素，即便是短距離區域航班亦然。此次客艙更新將使整體環境更感現代化，並讓波特成為首間在Dash 8飛機上使用此種增強客艙設計的加拿大航空公司。
Expliseat北美銷售副總裁Jean-François Tessier表示，此次合作反映雙方長期以來在創新座椅技術、輕量化性能、運營效率與乘客舒適度方面的共同承諾。波特航空的Dash 8-400飛機主要服務於加拿大東部及美國東北地區的區域航線，並與其日益增長的Embraer E195-E2噴射機隊互補。

en.title: Porter Airlines Upgrades Dash 8 Fleet with World's Lightest Seats
en.summary: Porter Airlines is fitting its entire fleet of 29 De Havilland Dash 8-400 turboprops with Expliseat TiSeat 2V ultra‑lightweight seats, the first upgraded aircraft already in service and the remainder to be completed by autumn 2026. The seats, made of carbon fibre and titanium, are claimed to be up to 30% lighter than conventional economy seats, reducing fuel burn and emissions. The refurbishment also adds LED mood lighting, new reading lights and fresh carpet while retaining the existing 2‑2 seat layout and pitch of 30‑32 inches.
body: Porter Airlines announced it is installing Expliseat TiSeat 2V ultra‑lightweight seats across all 29 of its De Havilland Dash 8-400 turboprop aircraft as part of a fleet‑wide cabin modernisation programme. The first upgraded aircraft have already entered service, with the remaining fleet slated for completion by autumn 2026.

Expliseat markets the TiSeat 2V as the world’s lightest aircraft seat in its category, constructed from carbon fibre and titanium. The manufacturer claims the seat can be up to 30% lighter than traditional economy seats, helping Porter lower fuel consumption and carbon emissions on its high‑frequency short‑haul routes.

In addition to the seats, Porter is equipping the Dash 8 fleet with LED mood lighting, new LED reading lights and fresh cabin carpeting. The airline says it is keeping the existing cabin layout unchanged, preserving 30‑inch pitch in PorterClassic and 32‑inch pitch in PorterReserve, and retaining the 2‑2 seat configuration with no middle seats.

Kent Woodside, Porter’s Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer, said passenger feedback identified seat comfort as a meaningful part of the travel experience, even on shorter regional flights. He added that the cabin refresh will noticeably renew the onboard environment and make Porter the first Canadian airline to operate Dash 8 aircraft with this enhanced cabin design.

Jean-François Tessier, Expliseat’s Vice President of Sales for North America, noted the upgrade reflects the companies’ long‑standing commitment to combining innovative seating technology with lightweight performance, operational efficiency and passenger comfort. Porter’s Dash 8‑400s serve regional routes across Eastern Canada and the northeastern United States, complementing its growing fleet of Embraer E195‑E2 jets on longer domestic and international sectors.
